title: §16-003: Testing Stream Pipelines & Event Emitters
description: Multiple-choice practice questions and deep runtime verification for §16-003 (Testing Stream Pipelines & Event Emitters).

cards.concept: Testing Stream Pipelines & Event Emitters: Test Doubles: Mocks, Stubs & Spies
cards.question: In automated testing, what is the exact conceptual distinction between a Stub and a Spy?

options.text: A Stub runs on the server; a Spy runs in the browser.
A Stub replaces a dependency with pre-programmed canned responses; a Spy records invocation details (arguments, call count, return values) without necessarily replacing behavior.
A Stub verifies security; a Spy benchmarks speed.
There is no difference.

cards.explanation: Stubs provide canned return values to isolate tested code from external side effects. Spies record execution telemetry to verify interactions.
cards.pitfall: Over-mocking internal implementation details rather than testing public interface contracts makes tests brittle to harmless refactoring.
cards.citation: Martin Fowler: Mocks Aren't Stubs / Node.js Mock API

cards.concept: Testing Stream Pipelines & Event Emitters: Integration Test Isolation & Database Cleanup
cards.question: What is the most reliable strategy to ensure database integration tests remain isolated and deterministic across parallel test runs?

options.text: Sharing a single permanent test database without cleanup.
Running each test within a rolled-back transaction or using ephemeral isolated database containers (Testcontainers) with schema truncation between suites.
Adding arbitrary sleep delays between tests.
Running integration tests exclusively in production.

cards.explanation: Transactional rollbacks or ephemeral database containers ensure test runs leave zero lingering state, preventing test order dependencies and flaky failures.
cards.codeSnippet:
beforeEach(async () => await db.query('BEGIN'));
afterEach(async () => await db.query('ROLLBACK'));
cards.pitfall: Failing to drain and close database connection pools in test teardown hooks causes test runners (Jest, node:test) to hang indefinitely.
cards.citation: Testing Best Practices: Ephemeral Test Environments
